findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and drops all DB deletes
findings.body: In the new cancellation block of the cron handler, the `await client.request(...)` to SendGrid is inside the `for` loop but the whole loop is wrapped in a single try/catch. If the SendGrid request fails for any one reminder (e.g. a stale/invalid `referenceId` batch_id, which returns an error from SendGrid), the loop exits immediately: (a) all remaining `remindersToCancel` never get their SendGrid cancellation posted, so those emails will still be sent even though the bookings were cancelled — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix; and (b) the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises collected in `workflowRemindersToDelete` are never awaited, and since Prisma promises are lazy, those deletes never execute. Because the failing row is never deleted, it will abort the loop again on every subsequent cron run (every 15 min), permanently blocking cancellations for all reminders that happen to sort after it (the query has no orderBy). Each reminder's SendGrid call and DB delete needs its own error handling so a single bad record can't block the batch.

findings.title: Reschedule path cancels SendGrid sends immediately and orphans the reminder rows, re-introducing the 100-pending-cancellations problem
findings.body: When a booking is rescheduled, the old booking's email reminders are cancelled via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete=true`. That path POSTs the `status: "cancel"` to SendGrid right away — for reminders that may be scheduled days in the future — which is exactly the behavior this PR identifies as the root cause of hitting SendGrid's max of 100 pending cancellations (pending cancellations accumulate until the scheduled date). Additionally, the immediateDelete path neither deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row nor sets `cancelled: true`, so the row lingers with `scheduled: true` and is invisible to the cron's `cancelled: true` cleanup; it only disappears when the generic `scheduledDate <= now` deleteMany runs after the send date. For consistency with the fix, the reschedule path should mark `cancelled: true` (like the cancel path in handleCancelBooking) and let the cron perform the SendGrid cancellation inside the final hour. Also note the whole forEach is fire-and-forget, so the surrounding try/catch can never catch errors from these async calls.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation writes are fire-and-forget and may be lost before commit
findings.body: Previously the cancel handler collected `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` promises into `remindersToDelete` and awaited them in `Promise.all`. The new code calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside a `forEach` without awaiting anything. The `cancelled: true` update (or row delete) therefore happens in the background after the response may already have been sent; in a serverless deployment the lambda can be frozen once the response completes, so the flag may never be written — in which case the cron never cancels the SendGrid send and the reminder email is still delivered, re-creating the bug this PR fixes. The calls should be collected and awaited (the same applies to the identical new pattern in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` requestReschedule and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`).

findings.title: Paid cancelled bookings return early and never cancel their workflow reminders
findings.body: When a paid booking is cancelled, the handler refunds the payment, sets the booking status to REJECTED, and returns early at `return { message: "Booking successfully cancelled." }` — before reaching the new "Workflows - cancel all reminders for cancelled bookings" block further down (which calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`). As a result, workflow reminders for refunded/cancelled paid bookings are neither flagged `cancelled` nor deleted, and SendGrid will still send the scheduled reminder emails — the exact issue this PR is meant to resolve, still reproducible for any paid event type. The reminder cancellation should happen before (or independent of) the paid-booking early return.

findings.title: requestReschedule cancels reminders without awaiting them
findings.body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, the old code collected `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises and awaited them via `Promise.all(remindersToDelete)`. The new code calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` in a `forEach` without awaiting. The mutation can complete and the serverless invocation can be torn down before the `cancelled: true` updates / deletes commit, leaving reminders active for a booking that was cancelled for rescheduling, so the cron never cancels them and emails may still be sent. The calls should be awaited.
